short: Skin-closed ECoG implant used at home without investigators (M13): standard, one user, skin-closed telemetry predates it; main-text 89% spelling accuracy pools inactive steps, no chance level.
position: The paper [@vansteensel2016] changes the device and its operation (M13): subdural ECoG with a subcutaneous transmitter, nothing through the skin after day 3, used at home without investigators from day 197. Both departures are standard: the skin-closed link predates it in the neurotrophic-electrode telemetry lineage [@guenther2009], and independent home use rests on one participant, though a [later] skin-closed study still calls it the only earlier unsupervised, ambulatory implantable BCI [@oxley2021]. The claim that one locked-in user can communicate without the team holds, and the [later] 7-year follow-up of the same user confirms durability, not generality [@vansteensel2024]. The main text's 89% spelling accuracy pools target and more numerous non-target steps with no chance level or false-click rate (M12); the same user's [later] night study shows unintended clicks are the failure that matters [@leinders2026]. At 1.8 letters per minute with word prediction, the rate is about 8 times below the first ALS user of the [later] endovascular system (inference) [@oxley2021].
